subject: How to specify an informed prior from historical data when regression parameters  are correlated

messages.author: c7a937bb95cf459b
messages.subject: How to specify an informed prior from historical data when regression parameters  are correlated
parts:
Hi INLA, 

Assuming informed priors for fixed effects are obtained from historical data and and regression parameters are correlated. 
How does someone specify co variance structure for the correlated regression parameters in subsequent analysis.

From  literature it is possible to apply  wishart distribution. However, I am facing challenges in trying to incorporate the correlations from historical data into new data model.

The sample code below gives details of what I aim to achieve:

require(INLA)

#data 1 (Historical data)
y<-rep(0:1, times=90)
x1<-rnorm(90,0.5,1)
x1f<-cut(x1,breaks=c(-3.5,0,4),labels=c("yes","no"))
summary(x1f)
x2<-as.factor(rep(c("A","B","C"),times=30))

data1<-data.frame(y=y,x1f=x1f,x2=x2)
head(data1)
attributes(data1$y)
#data 2 (Current Data)

y<-rep(0:1, times=60)
x1<-rnorm(120,0.4,1)
x1f<-cut(x1,breaks=c(-3.5,0,4),labels=c("yes","no"))
x2<-as.factor(rep(c("A","B", "C"),times=120))
data2<- data.frame(y=y,x1f=x1f,x2=x2)

#Model 1 based on historical data1

model1<-inla(y~x1f+x2,'binomial',control.compute = list(waic = TRUE),
             data=data1, control.family=list(link='logit'),
             control.fixed=list(correlation.matrix=TRUE,mean=list(x1fno=0,x2B=0,x2C=0),
                                prec=list(x1fno=0.001,x2B=0.001,x2C=0.001),
                                mean.intercept=0,prec.intercept=0),verbose = TRUE)
summary(model1)

#Extract Posterior estimates (mean and sd) for fixed effects from model 1 to be used as priors for model 2

#Extract posterior mean
post_mean<-model1$summary.fixed$mean 

#Exclude the posterior mean intercept
fixed_post_mean<-post_mean[-1] 

#Extract posterior sd
post_sd<-model1$summary.fixed$sd 

#Exclude posterior sd intercept 
fixed_post_sd<-post_sd[-1] 

# Variances for fixed effects in model 
fixed_post_var<-fixed_post_sd^2 

#Precisions for fixed effects in model
fixed_prec<-1/fixed_post_var 
#==================================================================================================================

#Data 2 analysis

#===================================================================================================================

#Using noninformative prior


model2<-inla(y~x1f+x2,'binomial',control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE),
             data=data2, control.family=list(link='logit'),
             control.fixed=list(mean=list(x1fno=0,x2B=0,x2C=0),
                                prec=list(x1fno=0.001,x2B=0.001,x2C=0.001),
                                mean.intercept=0,prec.intercept=0))
summary(model2)


# Using informative priors from model 1 in model 2 (data 2) assuming no correlations among fixed effects paramaters. 
# i.e b1 ~ dnorm( mub1 , 1/sb1^2 ) where b1 is for model 2 


model3<-inla(y~x1f+x2,'binomial',control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE),
             data=data2, control.family=list(link='logit'),
             control.fixed=list(mean=fixed_post_mean,prec=fixed_prec,
                                mean.intercept=0,prec.intercept=0))
summary(model3)

#Asssuming correlation among fixed effects correlations 

#The regression slope paramaters are modelled as B= [MU,SIGMA] where MU is a vector of MU=[mu_x1fno,mu_x2B,mu_x2C]
#and SIGMA is a covariance matrix of dimension 3 

#The covariance structure of model 1 is extracted from  model 1 using #correlation.matrix

#I wish to use wishart distribution- iid3d=== http://www.math.ntnu.no/inla/r-inla.org/doc/latent/iid123d.pdf to account for any correlations
#among regression paramaters in model 1 when used as informative priors for  data 2

#The main challenge I am facing is how to incorporate correlations for regression paramaters in the informative prior model under INLA formulation. 

I will greatly appreciate any suggestions. Thank you

On Tue, 2016-11-22 at 04:00 -0800, @e_stats wrote:
> Hi INLA, 
>
> Assuming informed priors for fixed effects are obtained from
> historical data and and regression parameters are correlated. 
> How does someone specify co variance structure for the correlated
> regression parameters in subsequent analysis.
>
> From  literature it is possible to apply  wishart distribution.
> However, I am facing challenges in trying to incorporate the
> correlations from historical data into new data model.
>

good question. in fact, there isn't an easy way to define a correlated
prior for the fixed effects. an easy way around is to use the
'rgeneric' model, but this seems not right either... 

If you happens to know the covariance matrix between the fixed effects,
like

.... X %*% beta + ...

and E(beta) = 0 and Cov(beta) = S, then you can always do 

S = V V'  and do a linear transform of X and beta into

XX %*% bbeta

where bbeta ~ N(0, I), and then transform the results back. in
control.fixed you can set a flag to get the posterior covariance for
the bbeta, and then just transform the results back to beta. 

I know, its not pretty....  it should be a model in itself.

H
